description:
In `src/ocaml/lib/ai_linter/crystal_rules.ml`, the function `detect_data_clump` is defined **twice** at lines 919 and 956. The OCaml compiler allows this (no warning emitted by default) and the second definition shadows the first.

**First definition (line 919) — broken:**
- Allocates `param_counts` hashtable (never used)
- Allocates `pair_counts` hashtable and populates it
- Then **falls off the end with no return value** — implicitly returns `()`, which is the wrong type for a `t -> (string * int) list` function

**Second definition (line 956) — working:**
- Skips `param_counts` entirely
- Populates `pair_counts`
- Folds hashtable into findings list, sorts and returns

The second one runs and produces correct findings, so the bug is invisible at runtime — but the first ~35 lines are dead code that will silently break if someone "fixes" the second one without noticing the first exists. It also signals sloppy maintenance: any future change to the logic could land in the wrong copy.

**Fix:**
- Delete the first definition (lines 919-953 plus the doc comment immediately above at 911-915)
- Keep the second, working definition

This ticket is a child of catseye-ozj (the refactor epic) but can land independently.
title: BUG: detect_data_clump defined twice — first version is silently broken
